In a social media post, he said the State’s growth rate in Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue had fallen below the national average under the TVK government. He also alleged that Korean investments worth ₹1,614 crore had been lost and gone to Andhra Pradesh because of the State government’s indifference.

“Guidance Tamil Nadu, which attracted investments, has been sacrificed because of the ego of individuals. One should learn from this government how to shift to reverse gear. But, the Chief Minister, who could not understand any of this, has gone to campaign in the byelections,” he said.

articles.title: Keralam govt. transfers 35 officers in major IAS reshufle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Keralam government has transferred 35 IAS officers in yet another major bureaucratic reshuffle.

K.R. Jyothilal, who was serving as Additional Chief Secretary of Finance, Taxes, and Public Procurement Advisory departments and as chief executive officer of the Rebuild Kerala Initiative in Planning and Economic Affairs department, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Home and Vigilance departments. He will also hold full additional charge of the Water Resources department, Housing department and Coir (Industries) department.

Puneet Kumar, who was serving as Resident Commissioner of Kerala House in New Delhi and Additional Chief Secretary of the Water Resources department (matters connected with inter-State water), has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Power department. He will also hold full additional charge of Officer on Special Duty in Coordination and Programme Management Division in the office of the Chief Secretary. He will continue as Resident Commissioner of Kerala House in New Delhi.
Tinku Biswal has been relieved from the additional charge of Officer on Special Duty in Coordination and Programme Management Division in the office of the Chief Secretary.

Minhaj Alam, Additional Chief Secretary of Home and Vigilance departments and Agriculture department, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Finance department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of Taxes and Public Procurement Advisory departments, and as chief executive officer of the Rebuild Kerala Initiative and chairman of the Kerala Financial Corporation.

Mohammed Hanish A.P.M., Additional Chief Secretary of Industries, Revenue (Waqf) and External Co-operation departments, has been posted as Additional Chief Secretary of the Health and Family Welfare department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of Ayush, General Education, Revenue (Waqf), and Minority Welfare departments.

Sharmila Mary Joseph, Principal Secretary of Health and Family Welfare and Ayush departments, has been posted as Principal Secretary of the Transport department. The officer will hold full additional charge of the Women and Child Development department.

M. Beena, on return from Central deputation, has been posted as Principal Secretary of the Industries department. The officer will also hold full additional charge of matters related to External Co-operation.

Prasanth N., Special Secretary of Sports and Youth Affairs, Zoos and Museum, and Taxes departments, has been posted as chairman and managing director of the Kerala State Electricity Board Limited. The officer will continue to hold charge as Special Secretary of the Sports and Youth Affairs department.

M.G. Rajamanickam, chairman and managing director of the Kerala State Electricity Board Limited and Secretary of Power and Environment departments, has been posted as Secretary of the Local Self-Government department. The officer will continue to hold additional charge of Revenue (Devaswom) department and Commissioner, Guruvayur and Koodalmanikyam Devaswoms.

Anupama T.V., Secretary of Local Self-government and Transport (Aviation, Metro and Railway) departments, and chairman and managing director of the Kerala Transport Development Finance Corporation, has been posted as Secretary of the Finance (Expenditure) department. The officer will also hold additional charge of the Environment department.
Gokul G.R. has been relieved from the charge of Finance (Expenditure) department and Geromic George from the charge of Finance (Expenditure) department.

articles.title: Government notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act; fixes 15-day deadline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Centre has notified rules for grievance redressal under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, mandating that complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme be resolved within 15 days and providing for their escalation if they remain pending beyond the prescribed period.

Under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Rural Development, state governments will have to establish a three-tier mechanism at gram panchayat, block and district levels, the Ministry said in a statement issued on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The rules provide for designated grievance redressal officers at each level to receive, register, enquire into and dispose of complaints.
According to the Ministry, grievances can be submitted in person, through speed post, a designated digital platform, telephone helplines or any other mode decided by state governments.
No grievance can be refused registration on the grounds of its format, language, manner of submission or any procedural deficiency, the statement said.

All complaints received physically at gram panchayat, block or district level will have to be entered on the designated digital platform on the day of receipt or, if that is not feasible, by the next working day.
The complainant will receive an acknowledgement with a registration number, date of receipt and designation of the receiving authority.
The rules stipulate that an enquiry into a grievance must be completed within seven working days of its receipt, while the complaint must be resolved within 15 days.

The designated officer can call for relevant records, documents, reports and electronic data from the authorities concerned and provide the complainant an opportunity to be heard, either in person or electronically, wherever necessary.

Complaints not resolved within 15 days will be escalated to the next higher level under the mechanism established by the state government. Such cases will continue to be monitored electronically until their disposal.
A district programme coordinator will oversee grievance redressal at the district level and ensure that complaints are addressed through the designated mechanism and digital infrastructure.

The rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism, in accordance with Schedule I of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025.

articles.title: PETA's plea: Celebrities, politicians, scientists sign against Centre's draft on animal cruelty rules
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several celebrities, politicians, scientists, veterinarians and animal welfare organisations have raised concerns over the proposed Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, with more than 18,000 people signing a petition seeking its withdrawal, according to People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) India.

Actors John Abraham, Tabu, Hema Malini, Raveena Tandon, Shilpa Shetty, Jacqueline Fernandez, Dia Mirza, Rupali Ganguly and Wamiqa Gabbi, among others, have signed the petition, while cricketer K.L. Rahul has also endorsed the appeal, PETA India said in a statement.

Several parliamentarians across political parties, including Lok Sabha MP Hema Malini, Rajya Sabha MP Sulata Deo, Lok Sabha MP Dr Mohammad Jawed and former Union Minister Renuka Chowdhury, have also signed the appeal, it added.

The appeal has also received support from more than 100 Indian and international scientists, over 100 veterinarians and more than 60 animal protection organisations, while over 18,000 people have signed a petition through PETA India's website, the statement said.
The proposal seeks to replace the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals (Control and Supervision) Rules, 1998.
It seeks to reduce bureaucratic delays and fast-track approvals of pharmaceutical, medical, and academic research through institutional self-regulation.

According to the Government, the draft rules actively strengthen animal welfare and ethical accountability while modernising scientific research. It has invited objections and suggestions till November 5.
But PETA India claims that the proposed rules, if notified in their present form, could weaken existing safeguards for animals used in laboratory experiments.
It added that the provisions could increase the capture and use of protected wildlife for experiments and allow community dogs and cats to be used in laboratories under specified circumstances.

The organisation also raised concerns over the continuation of experiments involving severe pain and distress, including inescapable electric shocks, induced tumours and toxicity tests in which death is an endpoint.

It further alleged that the draft rules would reduce oversight of the Central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) over several experiments and dilute existing safeguards relating to anaesthesia, euthanasia and rehabilitation.

"India has already demonstrated remarkable leadership in advancing non-animal science, and that is something every Indian can be proud of. We must build on this progress, not move backward," PETA India's science and research policy advisor Dr Noopur Jain said.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Heavy rain lashes Konaseema as cyclone Murasu nears Andhra coast
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. The wind speed during landfall is likely to be 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching 120 kmph. A storm surge of about 1.5-2 metres above the astronomical tide is very likely to inundate low-lying areas of South Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The maximum peak surge is expected in Bapatla and parts of Krishna and Prakasam districts.
He also warned that the storm surge could inundate low-lying areas even before landfall, as it is expected to begin three to four hours ahead of the cyclone’s landfall.
In the backdrop of the Murasu cyclone, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) 10th Battalion has undertaken extensive preparations.
It has deployed a total of 14 NDRF teams—11 from Andhra Pradesh and 03 from Tamil Nadu—to areas likely to be affected by the cyclone.

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm.
He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V.

Owing to waterlogging, several bus route roads in Chennai have started falling apart, as the northern and central regions of the city received widespread heavy rainfall due to Cyclone Murasu since Sunday (November 1, 2026) night.

A name rooted in Tamil’s cultural past is travelling across the Bay of Bengal as a weather warning. As the severe cyclonic storm advances towards the Indian coast, ‘Murasu ’ , a Tamil name suggested by the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has found its place in the region’s meteorological history.

With Cyclone Murasu likely to make landfall at Andhra Pradesh coast between evening of Monday (November 2, 2026) and early morning of Wednesday (November 3, 2026), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for two Telangana districts and an orange alert in three districts for Tuesday (November 3, 2026).
Cyclone Murasu has brought heavy rain to Konaseema in Andhra Pradesh, flooding homes and leaving elderly residents struggling.
Farmers are still recovering from damage caused by Cyclone Arnab, while power restoration has also been delayed.

The IMD said Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rain today (November 2), with isolated very heavy rain, and isolated heavy rain again on November 3 and from November 5 to 7.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay inaugurates new bus stand at Pudukottai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: On his maiden visit to Pudukottai after assuming office, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Monday distributed welfare assistance of ₹62.73 crore to 13,676 beneficiaries in the district and inaugurated the redeveloped new bus stand in the town.

Mr. Vijay inaugurated 44 completed projects worth ₹68.31 crore and laid the foundation for 70 new works worth ₹11.72 crore but did not address the gathering at the function organised by the district administration at the Collectorate.

The venue of the event, planned to be held at the District Armed Reserve grounds, was changed all of a sudden in the late hours on Sunday to the annexe building inside the sprawling District Collectorate premises where arrangements were made in a swift manner. Prior to that the Armed Reserve ground was being prepared on a feverish pace there to host the event.

Later, Mr. Vijay inaugurated the new bus stand that was redeveloped after the old structures were demolished and rebuilt at a cost of ₹23.25 crore. He went around the facility for about 15 minutes accompanied by his Cabinet colleagues, P. Madhusudhan Reddy, Director of Municipal Administration, and other officials.

Constructed by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply department on an area measuring 20,077 square metres, the new bus stand has 60 bays, 74 shops, a couple of restaurants, passenger waiting hall, and toilets. It has a police control room, a feeding room, and a reverse osmosis plant among other facilities.

The other projects inaugurated by the Chief Minister include the Arivusaar Maiyam (Knowledge Centre) constructed at Santhaipettai in Alangudi town panchayat and a seed storage godown at Vamban in Thiruvarankulam taluk.

Earlier, the Chief Minister, who arrived by a special flight at the Tiruchi International Airport from Chennai in the morning reached Pudukottai by road. Public and partymen lined up and cheered the Chief Minister at various points along the nearly 50-km Tiruchi-Pudukottai national highway stretch.

The Chief Minister reached the Pudukottai District Collectorate around 11.40 a.m. He was received by the Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and District Collector M. Aruna at the entrance of the annexe building. After receiving a guard of honour, Mr. Vijay had a look at the farm equipment kept on display and proceeded to the function venue.

Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources N. Anand, Lok Sabha MPs Durai Vaiko, S. Jothimani, and K. Navas Kani, Gandharvakottai MLA N. Subramanian and senior officials participated. After distributing welfare assistance to beneficiaries, Mr. Vijay received petitions from a few members of the public.

Thereafter, the Chief Minister proceeded on board his customised vehicle to the new bus stand in the town with crowds cheering him along the stretch braving the intense heat. A few of them standing near the bus stand fainted and were immediately shifted from the spot by the police personnel and given first aid.

The Kolkata-headquartered miner said that its supplies to the power sector also increased 19% to touch 57.1 MT. Overall supplies during the month surged 19% on a year-over-year basis to scale 70.3 MT. Both supplies to the power sector and overall supplies scaled record-highs in a single month, the company said.
About evacuation, it said that it loaded on an average 310 rakes per day — to the power sector — in October.

In a statement, the Coal India said, “The achievement assumes greater significance in view of the need to augment coal stocks at thermal power plants amid rising power demand, while disruptions caused by unseasonal rainfall, the Puja festivities and impact of a cyclone posed challenges to the operational performance.”

articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: GST collections jumped 23% year-on-year to the second-highest level of over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October as festive buying boosted domestic demand, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, , 2026).
October is the second consecutive month when monthly gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and second only to the record about ₹2.43 lakh crore mop-up in April.
Also, the 22.9% year-on-year growth clocked during the month is the fastest recorded pace of gross mop-up in the current fiscal year.
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
In April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

Grant Thornton Bharat, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Manoj Mishra, said October collections capture the festive-season demand cycle, which typically brings higher consumer spending, retail activity and movement of goods across sectors.
The performance across key states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, also points to continued strength in GST collections across major economic centres.

“The focus now should be on sustaining domestic revenue growth and ensuring that the benefits of GST 2.0 translate into stronger compliance, smoother input tax credit flows and faster refunds for businesses,” Mr. Mishra said.

EY India Tax Partner, Saurabh Agarwal, said the GST collections for October 2026 reflect the continued resilience of the Indian economy, despite persistent global headwinds. The steady month-on-month rise in revenue indicates strong underlying consumption and improving compliance.

articles.title: India’s coal imports decline 5.83% in August
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India’s overall import of coal fell 5.83% in August from the same period last year on the back of increased domestic production of the fossil fuel compound and reduced their shipments from overseas, according to government data.
The country imported 104.57 million tonnes (MT) of coal in August, compared to 111.05 MT in the same period last year.
Imports by domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants, that require the carbon-based compound for blending purposes, slumped 35.23% to 3 MT.
However, imports of thermal power plants that run solely on imported coal registered an uptick of about 1% at 18.31 MT.
Overall, coal imports by the power sector slumped about 6.4%.
The share of imported coal in India’s overall consumption basket declined to 19.3% in August this year compared to 21.2% in the same month last year.
Other than the power sector, coking coal, which serves as an important input for the steel industry, also declined about 4.2% during the reported period to 27.3 MT.
India depends on imports to meet 95% of its coking coal requirements. Import requirements are therefore subject to the demand of the steel sector.

Reflecting on the import dynamics, the Union Coal Ministry held, “The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure,” adding that imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

fullParagraphs: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was considering a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach. We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period," said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei.
He added that an exchange of messages was ongoing with the United States via mediators and that “everything depends” on the U.S. side accepting the Iranian demands.
Since the West Asia war broke out in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital energy conduit for shipping.
It regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross the strait without its authorisation, while the U.S. has in retaliation imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
In September, Iran initially proposed a seven-day plan that it conveyed to the U.S. through Qatar, which would have seen Tehran reopen Hormuz on the sixth day after the U.S. met Iranian demands.
Those demands include ending the West Asia war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the U.S. naval blockade.

In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday (November 1, 2026), Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transit through the strait.

articles.title: What are U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Every four years, halfway through a sitting president’s four-year term, the U.S. holds a nationwide poll known as the midterm elections. Although the White House occupant is not directly up for re-election in this vote, the outcome serves as a de facto referendum on the current administration’s leadership and political agenda.
The legislative branch, the U.S. Congress, is entirely at stake, as voters elect representatives to all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, who serve two-year terms.

At the same time, 35 of the 100 U.S. Senate seats which carry six-year terms are up for grabs (33 regular elections and two special elections in Florida and Ohio) alongside the state gubernatorial seats that decide chief executives across numerous states. Unlike centralised electoral systems, American voting, ballot printing, and counting are all decentralised, operating independently by local authorities and state governments across thousands of individual counties.

At the federal level, legislative power is divided between two chambers of Congress: the House of Representatives and the Senate. The House consists of all 435 members, each serving two-year terms, which means every seat in the chamber is recontested during every midterm cycle. In the Senate, members serve six-year staggered terms, with about one third of its 100 seats (most of the time 33-35 seats) up for vote. There are 100 U.S. senators, two from each state. Beyond Washington, state races also play an important role. Voters choose chief executives in gubernatorial elections across dozens of states along with the state lawmakers and local officials. These state governors hold executive authority over their respective jurisdictions and will be in office to manage the state governance during subsequent presidential elections.

The structure of U.S. government depends on a system of checks and balances. This is spread across the executive, legislative and judicial branches. When the President’s political party retains control over both the House and Senate, passing legislation and funding executive projects and handling other judicial appointments becomes relatively easier. However, if the opposing party gains a majority in even one chamber, it creates a divided government that can interfere the executive agenda.
Therefore, these midterms dictate whether a President spends their remaining two years in office advancing major policy initiatives or defending their administration against congressional pushback.

In the upcoming November 3 midterm elections, Republicans defend a narrow majority while democrats need a net gain of just a few seats to retake the House. Currently, Republicans have a 218-214 majority in the House, with two vacancies and one independent who caucuses with them. Meanwhile, Democrats are also striving to gain control of the Senate, where Republicans maintain a 53-47 majority. Some of the high-stakes races shaping this time’s midterms include:
* State gubernatorial races in key states such as California, Texas and Florida are also critical as winning governors will be in office during 2028 presidential elections.

The effects of U.S. midterm outcomes extend beyond its domestic borders. It can directly influence foreign policy, diplomatic relations, and even global trade. For India and other strategic partners, a shift in congressional leadership can change the direction of some critical legislative decisions including federal defence spending, regional security initiatives in the Indo-Pacifc and high tech transfers.

Especially, these midterm elections are arriving during a delicate phase in India-U.S. bilateral relations with an unratified interim trade framework and newly passed legislation threatening up to 100% tariffs on major purchasers of Russian energy, escalating tensions.

Moreover, with Indian nationals facing curbs on labour certification and visa extension policies, the upcoming congressional control can directly challenge the course of such policies, alongside international trade, tariffs and immigration rules.

Millions of citizens cast their ballots prior to election day through early in-person voting or postal mail-in ballots with more than 100 million people likely to cast ballots in this year’s midterm election. On polling day, voters mark their choices at local polling centres. Because mail-in processing guidelines and counting rules vary from state to state, final results can take several day to tabulate completely.

articles.title: Naftali Bennett’s ‘B’Yachad’ faction throws support behind Gadi Eisenkot to form next Israeli government

fullParagraphs: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett 's 'B’Yachad' faction has thrown its support behind Yashar party chief Gadi Eisenkot, announcing that it will recommend him to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government amid a political deadlock following Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) Knesset elections.
Mr. Bennett announced the decision in a post on X, saying he had promised throughout the election campaign to respect the voters' decision and was now acting accordingly.

"Throughout the entire election campaign, I promised to respect the decision of the voter, and that is what I am doing now. Therefore, I have decided that the 'Together' faction will recommend to the president to entrust the task of forming the government to Gadi Eizenkot. Good luck, Gadi!" Mr. Bennett said.
Responding to Mr. Bennett, Mr. Eisenkot thanked him for the support and said, "Together, we will bring Israel back to the right path!"

The development comes as Israeli President Isaac Herzog has urged political leaders to accept the election results and find creative solutions to prevent another election, with neither of the main political blocs securing a clear majority in the 120-member Knesset.

According to The Times of Israel , Herzog said he would receive the official election results on November 4 before beginning consultations with representatives of political factions at the President's Residence.

The election results gave the opposition 67 seats against 53 for the incumbent coalition. However, the Opposition bloc comprises 48 seats held by Zionist factions and 19 secured by Arab non-Zionist parties, presenting a challenge to coalition formation.
Mr. Herzog urged party leaders to "stop climbing up trees and face the reality" of the election outcome, calling for flexibility to break the political deadlock.
The newly elected Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10.

The campaign, conducted from November 2 to 8, has also begun in other parts of Pakistan, including Balochistan province, where vaccination teams are operating in 31 districts under heightened security measures.
The development comes a day after the National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication confirmed that the new case was reported from Khyber district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.
Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi said safeguarding vaccination teams has been heavily prioritised following past security incidents and attacks during immunisation drives.
Additional police personnel have been deployed in sensitive areas, while snap checking and mobile and motorcycle patrols have been increased to strengthen security, he said.
Anti-polio campaigns in Pakistan are regularly marred by violence.
Despite global efforts to eradicate the virus, challenges such as safety issues, vaccine hesitancy, and misinformation remain in eliminating it.

Vaccination efforts continue to face resistance from community members amid misinformation and religious concerns surrounding the vaccine, including false claims that it causes infertility or impotence.
In September, militants killed two policemen deployed to protect a polio vaccination team in Balochistan's Nushki district.
During the 2025 anti-polio campaigns in Karachi, the provincial health department documented approximately 41,000 instances where parents or guardians refused to vaccinate their children.
Pakistan and Afghanistan are the only countries in the world where polio remains endemic, according to the World Health Organisation.

articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

articles.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do.
Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH).
The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it.

The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession.

Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies.
Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis?
Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated.

Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH.
Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student?

Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment.

Williams: I think we’re starting to experience a major revolution in the field, and it is absolutely worth going into. Some people may not want to work in the field anymore; others may now feel motivated to.

Impagliazzo: I’m less confident. The rate of change is amazing. Until now, the same researchers mostly did both the glamorous part of research, solving, and the less glamorous part, verifying and explaining. Now it looks like much or most of the first will be done by AI, leaving humans the second -- until next year, when AI progresses further. I have no idea what research will be like next year.

fullParagraphs: A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.

Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

articles.title: Is there an alternative to corticosteroids to control vomiting during chemotherapy? A new study attempts to find out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting are among the most distressing side effects of cancer treatment in children. Preventing them is essential not only to improve quality of life, but also to help patients complete treatment. Yet the medicines used to prevent vomiting can themselves cause adverse effects, making the search for safe alternatives an important challenge in paediatric oncology.

An Indian multicentre clinical trial suggests that olanzapine may offer an alternative to dexamethasone, a corticosteroid routinely used to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting in children receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy — treatment with a high risk of inducing vomiting. The current regimen using dexamethasone is a guideline that is used regularly, but dexamethasone is a corticosteroid. The study was aimed at finding a comparable, non-corticosteroid option.

articles.title: What India’s leaky exam system can learn from Soviet shoe factories
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: While the protests in New Delhi, the Centre relenting, and the petitions at the Supreme Court bent the arc of justice towards the lakhs of students who had suffered from leaked examination papers, neither the Cockroach Janta Party-led opposition nor the ruling dispensation have offered any concrete steps to prevent future leaks, beyond administrative reshuffles and legislative amendments. Neither seems wiser than the other.

The operations of the National Testing Agency (NTA) bear an uncanny resemblance to those of state-owned shoe factories in Soviet Russia. Since these factories were not driven by consumer demand, factories could meet the required production quotas they got from above by producing N number of pairs within a narrow range of sizes, regardless of whether they lay unsold on the shelves. Sure, shoe prices had been kept frozen for decades, calculated as a percentage of the lowest government wage, but the shoes did not fit your feet. Workers and lower management had no incentives to be resource-efficient, and pilferage of leather, glue, and rubber was rampant.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.
• Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Citing GST revenue decline, Stalin says Tamil Nadu is ‘doomed’ under TVK government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: DMK president and former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Monday (November 2, 2026) said people should brace for difficult times as “Tamil Nadu was doomed” under the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.

In a social media post, he said the State’s growth rate in Goods and Services Tax (GST) revenue had fallen below the national average under the TVK government. He also alleged that Korean investments worth ₹1,614 crore had been lost and gone to Andhra Pradesh because of the State government’s indifference.

“Guidance Tamil Nadu, which attracted investments, has been sacrificed because of the ego of individuals. One should learn from this government how to shift to reverse gear. But, the Chief Minister, who could not understand any of this, has gone to campaign in the byelections,” he said.

articles.title: Government notifies grievance redressal rules under VB-G RAM G Act; fixes 15-day deadline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Centre has notified rules for grievance redressal under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, mandating that complaints related to the implementation of the rural employment scheme be resolved within 15 days and providing for their escalation if they remain pending beyond the prescribed period.

Under the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Grievance Redressal Rules, 2026, notified by the Union Ministry of Rural Development, state governments will have to establish a three-tier mechanism at gram panchayat, block and district levels, the Ministry said in a statement issued on Monday (November 2, 2026).
The rules provide for designated grievance redressal officers at each level to receive, register, enquire into and dispose of complaints.
According to the Ministry, grievances can be submitted in person, through speed post, a designated digital platform, telephone helplines or any other mode decided by state governments.
No grievance can be refused registration on the grounds of its format, language, manner of submission or any procedural deficiency, the statement said.

All complaints received physically at gram panchayat, block or district level will have to be entered on the designated digital platform on the day of receipt or, if that is not feasible, by the next working day.
The complainant will receive an acknowledgement with a registration number, date of receipt and designation of the receiving authority.
The rules stipulate that an enquiry into a grievance must be completed within seven working days of its receipt, while the complaint must be resolved within 15 days.

The designated officer can call for relevant records, documents, reports and electronic data from the authorities concerned and provide the complainant an opportunity to be heard, either in person or electronically, wherever necessary.

Complaints not resolved within 15 days will be escalated to the next higher level under the mechanism established by the state government. Such cases will continue to be monitored electronically until their disposal.
A district programme coordinator will oversee grievance redressal at the district level and ensure that complaints are addressed through the designated mechanism and digital infrastructure.

The rules also provide for appeals against orders passed under the grievance redressal mechanism, in accordance with Schedule I of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025.

articles.title: PETA's plea: Celebrities, politicians, scientists sign against Centre's draft on animal cruelty rules
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Several celebrities, politicians, scientists, veterinarians and animal welfare organisations have raised concerns over the proposed Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, with more than 18,000 people signing a petition seeking its withdrawal, according to People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) India.

Actors John Abraham, Tabu, Hema Malini, Raveena Tandon, Shilpa Shetty, Jacqueline Fernandez, Dia Mirza, Rupali Ganguly and Wamiqa Gabbi, among others, have signed the petition, while cricketer K.L. Rahul has also endorsed the appeal, PETA India said in a statement.

Several parliamentarians across political parties, including Lok Sabha MP Hema Malini, Rajya Sabha MP Sulata Deo, Lok Sabha MP Dr Mohammad Jawed and former Union Minister Renuka Chowdhury, have also signed the appeal, it added.

The appeal has also received support from more than 100 Indian and international scientists, over 100 veterinarians and more than 60 animal protection organisations, while over 18,000 people have signed a petition through PETA India's website, the statement said.
The proposal seeks to replace the Breeding of and Experiments on Animals (Control and Supervision) Rules, 1998.
It seeks to reduce bureaucratic delays and fast-track approvals of pharmaceutical, medical, and academic research through institutional self-regulation.

According to the Government, the draft rules actively strengthen animal welfare and ethical accountability while modernising scientific research. It has invited objections and suggestions till November 5.
But PETA India claims that the proposed rules, if notified in their present form, could weaken existing safeguards for animals used in laboratory experiments.
It added that the provisions could increase the capture and use of protected wildlife for experiments and allow community dogs and cats to be used in laboratories under specified circumstances.

The organisation also raised concerns over the continuation of experiments involving severe pain and distress, including inescapable electric shocks, induced tumours and toxicity tests in which death is an endpoint.

It further alleged that the draft rules would reduce oversight of the Central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) over several experiments and dilute existing safeguards relating to anaesthesia, euthanasia and rehabilitation.

"India has already demonstrated remarkable leadership in advancing non-animal science, and that is something every Indian can be proud of. We must build on this progress, not move backward," PETA India's science and research policy advisor Dr Noopur Jain said.

fullParagraphs: P.L.N. Murthy, Head of the Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the cyclone is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Narsapur, south of Ongole, between 11.30 p.m. on November 2 and 4 a.m. on November 3, 2026. Farmers are still recovering from damage caused by Cyclone Arnab, while power restoration has also been delayed.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay inaugurates new bus stand at Pudukottai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: On his maiden visit to Pudukottai after assuming office, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Monday distributed welfare assistance of ₹62.73 crore to 13,676 beneficiaries in the district and inaugurated the redeveloped new bus stand in the town.

Mr. Vijay inaugurated 44 completed projects worth ₹68.31 crore and laid the foundation for 70 new works worth ₹11.72 crore but did not address the gathering at the function organised by the district administration at the Collectorate.

The venue of the event, planned to be held at the District Armed Reserve grounds, was changed all of a sudden in the late hours on Sunday to the annexe building inside the sprawling District Collectorate premises where arrangements were made in a swift manner. Prior to that the Armed Reserve ground was being prepared on a feverish pace there to host the event.

Later, Mr. Vijay inaugurated the new bus stand that was redeveloped after the old structures were demolished and rebuilt at a cost of ₹23.25 crore. He went around the facility for about 15 minutes accompanied by his Cabinet colleagues, P. Madhusudhan Reddy, Director of Municipal Administration, and other officials.

Constructed by the Municipal Administration and Water Supply department on an area measuring 20,077 square metres, the new bus stand has 60 bays, 74 shops, a couple of restaurants, passenger waiting hall, and toilets. It has a police control room, a feeding room, and a reverse osmosis plant among other facilities.

The other projects inaugurated by the Chief Minister include the Arivusaar Maiyam (Knowledge Centre) constructed at Santhaipettai in Alangudi town panchayat and a seed storage godown at Vamban in Thiruvarankulam taluk.

Earlier, the Chief Minister, who arrived by a special flight at the Tiruchi International Airport from Chennai in the morning reached Pudukottai by road. Public and partymen lined up and cheered the Chief Minister at various points along the nearly 50-km Tiruchi-Pudukottai national highway stretch.

The Chief Minister reached the Pudukottai District Collectorate around 11.40 a.m. He was received by the Minister for Labour Welfare and Skill Development J. Mohamed Farvas and District Collector M. Aruna at the entrance of the annexe building. After receiving a guard of honour, Mr. Vijay had a look at the farm equipment kept on display and proceeded to the function venue.

Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources N. Anand, Lok Sabha MPs Durai Vaiko, S. Jothimani, and K. Navas Kani, Gandharvakottai MLA N. Subramanian and senior officials participated. After distributing welfare assistance to beneficiaries, Mr. Vijay received petitions from a few members of the public.

Thereafter, the Chief Minister proceeded on board his customised vehicle to the new bus stand in the town with crowds cheering him along the stretch braving the intense heat. A few of them standing near the bus stand fainted and were immediately shifted from the spot by the police personnel and given first aid.

articles.title: GST mop-up surges 23% to second-highest level of ₹2.31 lakh crore in October on festive demand boost
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: GST collections jumped 23% year-on-year to the second-highest level of over ₹2.31 lakh crore in October as festive buying boosted domestic demand, according to government data released on Sunday (November 1, , 2026).
October is the second consecutive month when monthly gross Goods and Services Tax (GST) crossed ₹2 lakh crore, and second only to the record about ₹2.43 lakh crore mop-up in April.
Also, the 22.9% year-on-year growth clocked during the month is the fastest recorded pace of gross mop-up in the current fiscal year.
Gross GST collections from domestic sales rose 16% to over ₹1.59 lakh crore, and revenues from imports climbed 42% to ₹72,246 crore.
The ₹2.31 lakh crore collection includes Central GST mop-up of 42,935 crore, State GST of ₹51,340 crore and Integrated GST of over ₹1.37 lakh crore, data showed.
Goods and Services Tax (GST) refunds increased 6.5% year-on-year to ₹27,934 crore in October.
After adjusting for refunds, net GST collections rose 26% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in October.
In April-October, gross GST collection grew 13.2% to over ₹14.77 lakh crore. Net collections rose 13% to over ₹12.69 lakh crore.

Grant Thornton Bharat, Partner and Tax Controversy Management Leader, Manoj Mishra, said October collections capture the festive-season demand cycle, which typically brings higher consumer spending, retail activity and movement of goods across sectors.
The performance across key states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, also points to continued strength in GST collections across major economic centres.

“The focus now should be on sustaining domestic revenue growth and ensuring that the benefits of GST 2.0 translate into stronger compliance, smoother input tax credit flows and faster refunds for businesses,” Mr. Mishra said.

EY India Tax Partner, Saurabh Agarwal, said the GST collections for October 2026 reflect the continued resilience of the Indian economy, despite persistent global headwinds. The steady month-on-month rise in revenue indicates strong underlying consumption and improving compliance.

fullParagraphs: India’s overall import of coal fell 5.83% in August from the same period last year on the back of increased domestic production of the fossil fuel compound and reduced their shipments from overseas, according to government data.
The country imported 104.57 million tonnes (MT) of coal in August, compared to 111.05 MT in the same period last year.
Imports by domestic coal-based (DCB) power plants, that require the carbon-based compound for blending purposes, slumped 35.23% to 3 MT.
However, imports of thermal power plants that run solely on imported coal registered an uptick of about 1% at 18.31 MT.
Overall, coal imports by the power sector slumped about 6.4%.
The share of imported coal in India’s overall consumption basket declined to 19.3% in August this year compared to 21.2% in the same month last year.
Other than the power sector, coking coal, which serves as an important input for the steel industry, also declined about 4.2% during the reported period to 27.3 MT.
India depends on imports to meet 95% of its coking coal requirements. Import requirements are therefore subject to the demand of the steel sector.

Reflecting on the import dynamics, the Union Coal Ministry held, “The decline in overall coal imports, particularly imports for blending at domestic coal-based power plants, underscores the importance of strengthening domestic production, transportation and supply-chain infrastructure,” adding that imports by imported coal-based power plants and the steel sector reflect their specific fuel and raw material requirements.

articles.title: Petrol export duty cut to nil, diesel levy raised by ₹3 a litre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government on Saturday (October 31, 2026) slashed the export duty on petrol to nil while hiking the levy on export of diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) by ₹3 per litre and 50 paise per litre respectively for the next 15-day period.
There was no change in the existing excise duty rates for petrol and diesel for domestic consumption.
Diesel exports would now draw a levy of ₹11.5 for every litre against ₹8.5 per litre it drew in the previous fortnight.
ATF would be subject to an export levy of ₹11 for every litre against ₹10.5 for every litre as mandated for the previous fortnight.
The revised levy on diesel assumes significance as India spiked its exports of the liquid vehicular fuel amid a global supply crunch, particularly in Europe.
According to data from real-time analytics provider Kpler, India’s diesel exports stood at 700 kilo barrels per day in October, the highest since September 2025.

Sumit Ritolia, Manager for Modelling and Refining at Kpler, in a social media post on Friday (October 30, 2026) further observed, “India’s diesel exports are expected to ease to 500-550 kbd in Nov–Dec as seasonal domestic demand peaks before recovering to 550–600 kbd in Q1 2027. Higher maintenance in Q2-27 will constrain export, with new capacity contributing meaningfully only later in 2027.”

The government has been conducting a fortnightly review of export levies since March 27, in the backdrop of the conflict in West Asia. These are done based on the average international benchmark prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF observed since the previous review.
This is to ensure the domestic availability of retail fuels by disincentivising exports.

India’s inflation is more stable now vis a vis 2010s though still uneven. Over the last decade, annual CPI inflation has averaged at about 5%, broadly within the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) 2-6% target band. Headline CPI fell to multi-year lows in 2025 but inflation edged up again by mid-2026 with September CPI at 5.54%. This is still high enough to erode real returns on low-yield assets.

fullParagraphs: Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

fullParagraphs: Iran's Foreign Ministry on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was considering a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. agrees to its conditions, having previously proposed a one-week timeline.

"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach. We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period," said Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei.
He added that an exchange of messages was ongoing with the United States via mediators and that “everything depends” on the U.S. side accepting the Iranian demands.
Since the West Asia war broke out in late February, Iran has claimed control over Hormuz, a vital energy conduit for shipping.
It regularly targets vessels that attempt to cross the strait without its authorisation, while the U.S. has in retaliation imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
In September, Iran initially proposed a seven-day plan that it conveyed to the U.S. through Qatar, which would have seen Tehran reopen Hormuz on the sixth day after the U.S. met Iranian demands.
Those demands include ending the West Asia war on all fronts, the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, lifting sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the U.S. naval blockade.

In an interview with Al Jazeera released on Sunday (November 1, 2026), Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington must accept a new route agreed between Iran and Oman for transit through the strait.
